question: Can a fixed small validation budget distinguish wrong numerical rays by independent coefficient rank or measured counts?
outcome: On KHI-04's reused 200 four-swap worlds, greedy rank rejects nine wrong rays with two checks and a counted unit anchor, or three checks without scale. Count-first needs one anchored count or two unanchored counts. Three account-first checks leave one wrong ray. Filtering collective ambiguous sets gives 199 correct absolute points and one rejected world under the stated policies.
challenge: One unanchored count fits every wrong ray by changing scale; account checks can repeat the same rank-one relation. Acquisition costs and measurement error are unavailable in this fixed generated population.
remedy: Freeze a post-outcome equal-check-count comparison, seal selector rows before opening targets, retain points/rays/positive families and compute exact random-subset expectations. Independently audit 33,600 deterministic records, 59,856 random-family intersections and compatible wrong witnesses.
retry_when: Fresh prospectively selected objects supply measured check costs, uncertain counts or incomplete validation membership.
